evidence: M-O s.v. Christian: Ascension (Day): diēs Ascēnsiōnis Chrīstī in caelum (Tursellinus, 1652)
terms.comment: Classically an ascent (ascēnsiō, Plaut.; Lewis & Short); the feast forty days after Easter, a Thursday, in both churches. Lewis & Short do not give the feast’s name.

phrases.latin: assūmptus est in caelum, et sedet ā dextrīs Deī
phrases.english: he was taken up into heaven, and sits at the right hand of God

phrases.latin: ēgressus ejus ā Patre, regressus ejus ad Patrem, excursus ūsque ad īnferōs, recursus ad sēdem Deī
phrases.english: his going out from the Father, his going back to the Father, his journey down to the dead, his return to God’s throne

sources: Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. Christian: Ascension (Day).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-augustinus), checked against the editions named there.
Vulgate verses checked against the Clementine Vulgate (CrossWire VulgClementine, via the scrollmapper bible_databases repository) and Hetzenauer’s edition, in Clementine spelling.
